1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
In Peñaseca it had been raining for three days. That spring, Lucía Romero's older sister had left for Madrid, and since then Lucía had been running the village's small apothecary alone.
At nightfall she closed the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone knocked hard on the downstairs door. A man's voice called out, "Is anyone there?"
On the threshold stood a young man soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in a bloodstained cloth. He said his name was Diego Lobo and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need someone to treat me," Lobo said quietly. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred reales be enough?"
He took from his jacket a letter wrapped in waxed paper. "This letter must reach the monastery of San Blas before the eighteenth of May."
For Lucía, healing the wound was child's play, but the letter troubled her.
Still, she refused his money and simply said, "At dawn tomorrow I'll take you to the mountain."
2: At daybreak they set out. Lucía carried a basket on her back with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope they met old Tomás Gil, who was chopping firewood. He set down the axe and told them in a low voice that the previous evening three strangers had asked at the entrance to the village about a wounded young man.
“Take the path, Lucía,” said Tomás Gil. “The main road isn’t safe.” Lucía thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Lucía went first, planting her feet firmly with every step. Lobo followed in silence.
At noon the rain stopped, the fog slowly lifted, and in the distance the roof of the monastery of San Blas appeared. A nun was waiting at the door, Sister Inés, in charge of receiving visitors.
Sister Inés took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. “The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years.”
Lobo said to Lucía, “I owe her my life.” Lucía smiled. “Then next time you come, fix the roof of the apothecary for me.” Lobo stayed at the monastery.
At dusk Lucía came down the mountain alone. When she got home it was already night; she lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long time.
